TEXT_C:
SNP Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core stance
- Make Scotland stronger at Westminster with a louder, progressive voice.
- Oppose austerity; never put the Tories into power. If there’s an anti‑Tory majority, work with others to keep them out and press Labour for real change.
- Independence isn’t the focus of this election; it’s about better governance for Scotland and the UK.

Economy and public finances
- Replace deep cuts with modest, responsible spending increases and major infrastructure investment; borrowing and debt fall as a share of GDP.
- Fairer taxation: restore 50p top rate; tax bankers’ bonuses; raise bank levy; mansion tax; abolish non‑dom status; crack down on avoidance; review pension tax relief; reverse married couples’ allowance.
- Create a sovereign wealth (energy) fund when feasible.
- Seed‑fund the Scottish Business Development Bank; expand export finance; protect small firms with prompt‑payment laws; stabilize and consider extending the Annual Investment Allowance; raise the Employment Allowance to £6,000 by 2019–20.

Jobs, pay and welfare
- Raise minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020 (with higher youth/apprentice rates than today); promote the Living Wage and equal pay audits.
- End exploitative zero‑hours practices via consultation with unions and business.
- Scrap the Bedroom Tax; halt Universal Credit and PIP rollout; reverse DLA-to-PIP; increase UC work allowance by 20%; overhaul sanctions and disability assessments; raise Carer’s Allowance to JSA level.
- Protect pensioners: triple lock; single‑tier pension at £160/week; review rise in state pension age; keep winter fuel allowance.

Public services, health and housing
- Increase UK health spending by £24bn above inflation by 2020–21, delivering c.£2bn more for Scotland; protect NHS from privatisation; invest in mental health, integration of health and social care, delayed discharges and new medicines.
- Childcare: move to 30 hours/week free nursery for all 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds.
- Education: 30,000 Modern Apprenticeships annually by 2020; expand EMA; keep university tuition free.
- Housing: back 100,000 affordable homes per year UK‑wide; expand building in Scotland.

Energy, environment and bills
- Cut energy bills by funding ECO from general taxation; ensure wholesale price falls are passed on; protect pre‑payment customers.
- Strong climate targets; support a Climate Justice Fund; expand Green Investment Bank.
- Boost renewables (offshore/onshore, hydro, CCS); transmission reform; island interconnectors; moratorium on fracking; expand community energy/heat.
- Oppose Trident renewal and save up to £4bn a year in mid‑2020s.

Infrastructure and regions
- Prioritise HS rail linking Glasgow/Edinburgh with the North of England; build from north and south; accelerate broadband/4G with a Universal Service Obligation.
- City Deals for all Scottish cities and a £300m Scottish Cities Fund; “northern focus” for UK investment.
- Fair share of CAP convergence uplift; protect Royal Mail’s universal service; explore return to public ownership.

Rights, democracy and governance
- Deliver Smith Commission in full, then move to full fiscal responsibility; prioritise devolution of welfare, employment, business taxes, NI and equalities.
- EU: oppose withdrawal; require a “double majority” for any exit; protect public services from TTIP.
- Democratic reform: STV for Commons; scrap House of Lords; meaningful MP recall; votes at 16; protect Human Rights Act and ECHR; oppose mass surveillance; devolve broadcasting and secure a fair BBC Scotland share (+£100m).

Foreign, defence and justice
- Parliamentary oversight of military action; recognise Palestine; keep aid at 0.7% GNI; appoint an LGBT+ rights envoy.
- Defence without Trident; strengthen Scotland’s conventional footprint (maritime patrol aircraft, patrol vessels); build Type 26 in Scotland; better veteran support.
- Keep 1,000 extra police; seek VAT exemption for Police and Fire; retain Scottish court fines; regulate payday lenders; devolve powers over Fixed Odds Betting Terminals.

TEXT_E:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core vision: Secure a strong economy to fund public services and improve life “at every stage,” rewarding work, spreading opportunity, and keeping Britain safe.

Economy and tax
- Eliminate the deficit, run a surplus from 2018–19, and keep debt falling; no rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance.
- Raise Personal Allowance to £12,500 and higher-rate threshold to £50,000; new “Tax-Free Minimum Wage” link so 30 hours on the Minimum Wage pays no Income Tax.
- Crack down on tax evasion/avoidance; keep competitive business taxes and simplify the system.

Jobs and business
- Create 2 million more jobs and achieve full employment; support small firms via business rates review, red tape cuts, prompt payment, Start Up Loans, and export support.
- Deliver 3 million new apprenticeships; abolish employers’ NICs for apprentices under 25; tackle long‑term youth unemployment with a time‑limited Youth Allowance and “earn or learn” requirements.

Infrastructure and regional growth
- Over £100bn infrastructure investment: HS2/HS3, rail electrification, Crossrail, £15bn for roads, cycling and ultra‑low emission vehicles.
- Universal superfast broadband to 95% by end‑2017; improve mobile coverage and lead on 5G.
- Build a “Northern Powerhouse” and devolve powers/budgets to cities with elected mayors.

Housing
- Double first‑time buyers; extend Help to Buy and introduce Help to Buy ISA.
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount for under‑40s), 275,000 additional affordable homes; extend Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants; prioritize brownfield and protect the Green Belt.

Welfare and childcare
- Reduce household benefit cap to £23,000; freeze working‑age benefits for two years (key exemptions); roll out Universal Credit.
- 30 hours’ free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds; tax‑free childcare up to £2,000 per child.

NHS and social care
- Increase NHS spending every year; at least £8bn extra by 2020 to deliver a 7‑day NHS and same‑day GP access for over‑75s.
- Integrate health and social care (Better Care Fund); focus on mental health, cancer, dementia; expand digital access and transparency.

Education and skills
- Protect per‑pupil funding; zero tolerance of failing/coasting schools; expand academies and free schools (500 new).
- Tougher standards in literacy/numeracy; core academic GCSEs; 17,500 extra maths/physics teachers; no cap on university places; new postgraduate loans; expand technical routes (UTCs, Degree Apprenticeships).

Immigration
- Target net migration in the tens of thousands.
- EU reforms: four‑year residency before in‑work benefits/social housing; end child benefit for children abroad; tougher deportation and re‑entry rules; stronger enforcement and action on illegal working.

Law, security and rights
- Complete police reform; modernize prisons; new Victims’ Law; tougher sentences for serious crime.
- Counter‑extremism powers (banning/extremism disruption orders); update communications data laws.
- Replace the Human Rights Act with a British Bill of Rights.

Energy and environment
- Keep bills down via competition and smart meters; support shale with community benefits; back nuclear and value‑for‑money renewables; end new subsidies for onshore wind and give locals final say.
- Meet climate commitments cost‑effectively; protect nature with a “Blue Belt,” plant 11m trees, improve air/water, expand flood defences.

Pensions and older people
- Keep triple lock; introduce single‑tier pension; protect pensioner benefits; cap residential care costs; raise effective Inheritance Tax threshold on the family home to £1m for couples.

Constitution, EU and foreign policy
- English votes for English laws; implement new powers for Scotland and Wales; support NI settlement.
- Hold an in/out EU referendum by end‑2017; reform EU, protect Single Market, keep the pound.
- Maintain strong Armed Forces (retain Trident), meet NATO commitments, and spend 0.7% GNI on international development.
